_comment: File-by-file provenance for this port. Every mapping below was checked against the source tree at the commit named in `source`, not inferred from names alone; `basis` records what the check was. Licence terms are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

port.shape: 18 markdown agent prompts plus 5 standard-library Python scripts
port.principle: The prompts do the thinking. The Python does bookkeeping only: citation compilation, an integrity gate, assembly, export. No model call lives in the Python layer.
port.license: Apache-2.0 (this bundle); the derived work retains the upstream MIT notice

license.licensed_work: Floom's contributions to this bundle are licensed under Apache-2.0. Material derived from OpenDraft retains its MIT copyright and permission notice in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
license.copyright_holder: Floom (bundle contributions); SCAILE Technologies GmbH (OpenDraft-derived material)
license.note: The Apache-2.0 terms in LICENSE are the upstream bytes unmodified except for the appendix copyright line, and they match the other public Floom Skill bundles byte for byte. OpenDraft identifies its licence as MIT and names SCAILE Technologies GmbH as the 2025 copyright holder; that complete notice is retained in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. EVALS.md reports measured runs of this bundle against an identical agent with nothing loaded; read it there, and read no quality or Trust state into this grant.

hash_scope: copy_files lists every file this bundle ships except DERIVATION.json, because a record cannot contain its own hash. copy_files_sha256 is the sha256 of 'path:sha256' lines in path order, one per line, each terminated by a newline, which is the recipe the other bundles in this repository use. Upstream material left unported is listed in not_ported.
source_files_note: Empty on purpose. The other bundles here are copies of a private original, so they hash that original file by file. This one is not a copy. Every file was written for this bundle against the upstream project named in `source`, which is pinned by commit rather than by a file list. Nothing was taken byte for byte, so there is no source file whose hash would carry meaning. The file-by-file mapping to upstream is in agents and scripts below.

agents.basis: name match; engine/phases/compose.py header reads 'Compose phase - 7 Crafter agents writing thesis sections'

scripts.basis: citation_compiler.py header: 'Replaces {cite_001} with formatted citations ... generates reference lists'; citation_database.py header: 'schema validation, loading, and saving for citation databases'; citation_verifier.md is titled 'Agent #14: Citation Compiler' and describes 'Deterministic citation ID replacement using citation database', so it is carried here as code rather than as a nineteenth prompt.
scripts.note: Placeholders are keyed by DOI ({cite_<doi>}) rather than by ordinal ({cite_001}), so a renumbered database cannot silently repoint a marker at a different work.

scripts.basis: quality_gate.py header: 'Quality gate for draft output scoring'.
scripts.note: Re-scoped from scoring to checking. The upstream gate produced a quality score; this one answers pass/fail on mechanical properties (orphan markers, unresolved DOIs, unfilled bracket slots, word bands) and adds an advisory number-provenance report that never changes the exit code.

scripts.basis: compile.py header: 'Compile and export phase - assembly, abstract, PDF/DOCX export'. Only the assembly half is carried here.
export_professional.py header: 'Production-grade academic document export utility ... multiple PDF engines (LibreOffice, Pandoc, WeasyPrint) with auto-fallback'.
scripts.note: Reduced to standard-library Markdown and HTML output. The upstream PDF engines are third-party binaries and are not a dependency of this bundle.

scripts.basis: orchestrator.py header: 'Citation research orchestrator with intelligent fallback chain ... Coordinates Crossref -> Semantic Scholar -> Gemini Grounded -> Gemini LLM for 95%+ success rate'. That directory reads SERPER_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY and OPENALEX_API_KEY.
scripts.note: Rewritten against Crossref and OpenAlex only, both keyless, with DOI resolution at Crossref and DataCite. No API key and no account are required anywhere in this bundle. The upstream chain's last two links are dropped rather than reimplemented: a language model asked to supply a citation when the indexes return nothing is the exact failure this pipeline exists to refuse, and a 95% success rate bought that way is 5% invented sources.

not_ported.reason: Titled 'COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH PLANNER - Autonomous Literature Review Strategy'. Its planning role is covered by the four scoping questions in SKILL.md and by stage 1's own query plan.
Claim extraction as a separate LLM pass. This bundle checks claims against sources inside stage 11 and mechanically in scripts/integrity.py, rather than as two more prompt stages.
The judging half of the same two-pass factcheck; see above.
Carried into scripts/citations.py as code. Its own description is 'Deterministic citation ID replacement', which is work a script does exactly and a model does approximately.
Digest output format, outside the paper pipeline.
TLDR output format, outside the paper pipeline.
Orchestration document. SKILL.md is this bundle's equivalent.

deliberate_corrections: Word-count floors removed. A floor rewards padding, and a section that comes in short is reporting thin evidence rather than failing a quota.
AI-detection-evasion targets removed. Writing to defeat a detector is not a quality axis.
Year approximation removed. A guessed publication year is a fabricated citation.
Pre-filled 'p < 0.05' removed from templates. A significance threshold printed before any analysis is a number waiting to be adopted.
The title-scoring rubric removed. It scored titles against a formula rather than against the paper.

edits.note: docx typography now lands on pandoc 3.1.x: the section-properties patch accepts the self-closing <w:sectPr /> that older pandoc ships, and a failed margin patch no longer discards a font and size patch that succeeded. Added an end-to-end test that invokes the host's real pandoc instead of a hand-written XML fixture.

Renamed from `opendraft` to `autonomous-research` so the Skill name describes what it does rather than carrying a project name. Folder, front-matter `name:` and the SKILL.md title changed; the body still credits OpenDraft as the upstream project, and the OpenDraft MIT notice is unchanged.

EVALS.md published for this Skill, and the licence note no longer says that no evaluation has been run, because one has. The page reports two runs: one on the tasks the Skill was written beside, which resolved, and one on held-out tasks, which did not.
